title: fix(cloud): explain missing macOS and Windows choices on older Crabbox
body:
Related: #142095, #142679, #143463.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users opening the cloud operating-system picker could not see macOS or Windows choices when the installed Crabbox binary was too old or its version could not be verified. The same omission left Cloud Workers settings without an explanation or upgrade path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep provider-advertised unavailable operating systems in the catalog with a bounded, optional repair explanation. New Session, Move, and Cloud Workers settings show those choices disabled; session pickers wrap the explanation below the OS name. Provider version requirements, machine filtering, and provisioning rejection remain enforced. The generic catalog contract carries availability; Crabbox owns its version policy.

This intentionally expands discovery responses to include unavailable choices. Catalog consumers should honor the optional `disabledReason`; the maintained pickers are updated together and allocation checks remain independent. No configuration, stored record, SQLite schema, or persisted default changes, so no data migration is required.

## User Impact

Users can see why an OS is unavailable and that upgrading Crabbox and restarting the Gateway enables supported choices. Linux selection and dispatch retain their existing behavior. Configured provider defaults remain intact.

## Evidence

The regression failed on the original behavior. Focused provider, service, discovery, draft selection, settings, and Move tests passed. A browser E2E verifies unavailable OS names and repair text remain readable, choices are disabled, and Linux dispatch omits an OS override. The production UI bundle built successfully. Final provider validation passed 301 tests, the SDK contract test passed, and core/test, UI, and extension/test typechecks passed. Final targeted extension lint and the remaining selected architecture guards passed. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.

Post-merge live verification passed on deployed commit `1c72b612a852d7d5ae7cc8615748d19a9cb8a9ad` with Crabbox 0.55.0: native Windows on Azure and macOS on AWS both update the selected placement and machine lists. Windows (WSL2) selection was also verified during the operational repair. The served UI asset changed, build identity matched, and health/readiness/startup, channels, session reads, and Workboard reads passed with a stable process generation. This verifies the picker flow; no live worker allocation is claimed. [Final CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34449673497).

The captures below use synthetic catalog data. The before capture shows the previous catalog omission; the after capture shows the same picker with unavailable choices and repair instructions.
